correctness.rationale: For the specified fixed point, p_(2i)=0 and p_(2i+1)=1−p_i. Thus 11 is forbidden, and four consecutive zeros would include two successive odd positions and force 11 in the parent. For odd n≥5, two ones on a Lie-class circle produce separations d and n−d in two rotations; they cannot both be even. With at most one one, some rotation instead contains 0000. For 2m with m≥2, a qualifying word contains a one, and all ones have one parity. Rotating to odd support gives a unique aligned μ-image. Every even rotation remains aligned in the fixed point, because a relative odd-position one forces an even starting index; hence all the decoded rotations occur. Conversely, aligned occurrences of every even rotation of an image always have a following zero, giving all the odd rotations too. Odd shifts cannot identify distinct aligned μ-image classes with nonempty one-support, so this is a bijection. Directly L(1)=L(2)=L(3)=2, with length-two classes [00],[01] and length-three classes [000],[001]. This proves the positive-length formula; the two supports are disjoint, and their geometric bounds give the stated count and lacunary series. The empty-word convention is separate. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_math_checks.py checks exact factor sets and all class representatives through n=200 using a recursive parent-factor language, without any inferred prefix cutoff. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed; agreement of two finite prefixes would not on its own prove completeness, as VERIFICATION.md also notes. The symbolic argument covers all lengths.
